书接上回，接着聊昨晚聊的多端技术选型，今天我们来聊第二篇，说说我是怎么在 Mac 上来开发原生 Windows 软件的，以及我是如何搭建编译、测试环境的，还有最近一个月做 Mole Windows 版踩过的一些有意思的坑。

技术栈上，Mac 版本的 Mole 使用的也是原生的 Swift + SwiftUI，能够让我很好调用系统能力以及非常好的性能体验，想着不将就，所以在 Windows 上我也是想着直接用本身写 Windows 软件最直接的语言， C# 加 WinUI 3，跑在 .NET 10 上，过程虽然难搞，但是相比十年前我了解轮子哥谈的 Windows 开发要简单好理解一些了。

Windows 上的原生界面框架其实挺多的，包括很多年前了解过的 Win32、WinForms、WPF、UWP 这一波，WPF 是 2006 年出的，到现在还在维护，但控件和设计语言不是很好看，非常上一代的感觉，然后 UWP 又被沙盒和应用商店给绑定住，现在微软主推的是  Windows App SDK 里的 WinUI 3，界面框架从系统里面拆出来单独发版，这样就有一个好处，普通的 Win32 程序也能用，基础组件就是 Windows 11 自己的 Fluent 风格，我还挺喜欢，高分屏缩放和 ARM64 都是原生支持。

然后这里 .NET 10 是去年 11 月发的长期支持版本，打包时我把运行时一起打进去，用户不需要另外装 .NET，x64 和 ARM64 这里各出了一个原生安装包，骁龙的 Windows 笔记本就不要走转译了，相当于尽量让用户使用简单不折腾。这里安装和更新用的是开源的 Velopack 框架，可以很方便做增量更新，也很好用。

工程师开始写代码时候肯定会想到能复用尽量复用，所以我开始写的时候也非常想复用 Mac 的 Swift 代码，后面让 AI  分析了一下，十几万行代码 Swift 代码可以脱离  AppKit、SwiftUI 这些系统框架使用的20%都没有，处理的逻辑也是  ~/Library  这类 macOS自己的路径规则，基本用不上，所以  Windows 版几乎是从零开始写的。

两边的关系其实非常简单，外观和交互我尽量完全一致，尽可能让大家意识里面认为的 Windows 软件不那么精致美观的感觉在这里也保持我认为好的水平，然后底层代码各写各的，关于视觉的一致性还原有了AI以后很简单，我把原本的 Mac 版写在 Swift 里的颜色、字号、间距、圆角这些设计 token，直接写了一个脚本生成为 Windows 里面XAML 资源，文案也是从 Mac 的多语言文件转成 Windows 的格式，11 种语言一起转过来，甚至大家看到的菜单栏里面的那个runner动画也是用的同一个脚本同步来的。

虽说同步，可能大家会觉得很简单，其实这里需要花点精力防止 AI 直接给你跑偏了，每次同步其实我会记录对应的是Mac的哪一个提交，这样两边就不会走偏去，然后功能上会有一份 SYNC.md 当做对账表，Mac 每加一个功能、修一个安全问题，Windows 这边都会标清楚哪些是已经实现、哪些是刻意不同还是不适用，以及为什么这样判断。

通过这两个机制，我可以很好的让两边的底层完全各写各的，但是又能很好地保持功能对齐，完全不需要刻意去硬写一层兼容去磨平，反而会变复杂，这里能复用的反而是设计、文案以及踩坑后定下来的各种规则，反而这些是 AI 非常喜欢的“能力抽象层”，也就是说随着时代发展，慢慢所谓的代码抽象没有那么重要了，反而是规则抽象更重要。

另外 Windows 开发还有一块比 Mac 要麻烦不少，就是证书签名，没有签名的，一打开会出现「Windows已保护你的电脑」，甚至 Windows 11 的智能应用控制会直接不让运行，国内不少安全软件也会把没签名的程序当成可疑报毒，这和 Mac 上没签名、没公证的软件提示「已损坏」差不多，平时 Mac 上大家还可以跑一条命令解掉，Windows 上想正规分发，这一步没有啥好办法，就是需要。

调研下来微软的签名生态的确比苹果差太多了，微软有自己的 Azure Artifact Signing，一个月 9.99 美元最省事，居然个人只开放给美国和加拿大的开发者，没办法使用，很奇葩的规定，然后行业还规定从 2023 年起签名私钥必须放在硬件或者云端 HSM 里，不能再是电脑上的一个文件，今年起单张证书最长只能用 460 天，差不多一年多就得换一次证书

最后我买的是 Certum 的云端 OV 证书，3 年 3百多美元，签名时登录电脑上的 SimplySign，再用手机上的 App 给一个动态码，SmartScreen 的信誉也跟着证书上审核过的名字慢慢积累。刚开始一段时间的签名包在 ThinkPad 上也会一样被 SmartScreen 拦了下来，后来我每次发版都把安装包提交到微软的恶意软件分析门户，让信誉慢慢积累起来，而且 SimplySign 的登录会话闲置几个小时就会断开，需要再次输入动态码才能继续签名，所以这里其实很难做成云端自动打包。

证书搞定后，就是开发环境的事情了，我的研发要求是代码和 AI 的上下文必须全留在 Mac 上，Mac 用习惯了，真的很难使用 Windows 去研发，这里 Windows 只负责编译和验证效果和各种测试，所以我在 Mac 上装了 Parallels Desktop，大概 3 百多块一年，之前也挺不少小伙伴吐槽过这个软件，不过在我的 M5 Pro 上跑 Windows 11 还挺顺滑，让我感觉这个钱花得很值。

它最好用的一点是我的 Claude 能很顺手地操作它，仓库直接作为 Parallels 的共享文件夹挂进虚拟机，变成一个 X 盘，Mac 上改完代码，虚拟机里直接编译，不需要来回 Copy 文件，只是两边的编译产物要分到不同的目录，对于编译、启动、看日志的工作都被我写成了脚本，通过 Parallels 自带的 prlctl exec 直接在虚拟机里执行，程序启动就崩的时候 Windows 只给一个 0xc000027b，Mole 会把真正的异常写进日志，脚本跑完顺手打印出来，Claude 直接就能读到。相当于写代码还是在 Mac 上的 Claude Code 里，调试和运行都在虚拟机里，脚本不能解决的地方，直接用 Codex 的 computer use 去点，只有少部分那种系统确定弹框点不了，我在这里就是这个职责，点点系统弹框确定，哈哈。

说到这里，可以和大伙分享一下 Mole Windows的架构分层，一共四层，最底下的 Core 只依赖 .NET，不碰任何 Windows 接口，清理规则、路径安全检查、卸载残留的判断都放到这里，测试用的是一个按 Windows 路径规则模拟出来的内存文件系统，这样在 Mac 上也可以很好的跑；往上是 Platform 层，注册表、文件系统、Win32 调用这些真正的系统接口都放在这一层，打开 EnableWindowsTargeting 以后，Mac 上也能编译通过；再往上就是写过应用同学非常熟悉的界面状态的 ViewModel 层，这里和 Mac 版本会一一对应，这样也能够在 Mac 上测，只有最上面这一层的 WinUI 界面必须去 Windows 里编译。

这也是让我一个月时间可以写8 万多行 Windows 代码、4000 多个测试，但是几乎大部分可以在 Mac 上完成的一个很方便的地方，也是架构设计的巧妙处，当然这里我只提供之前做架构时候的想法建议，大部分是 Opus 5.5 去帮我整的，很牛逼。

接着可以聊测试了，我反而认为 在 AI 时代，工程师最大的价值，除了架构设计外就是这个测试验证了，所以为了保证产品是可以售卖的，肯定需要在真实环境测试验证，反复找体验问题去修复的，所以我整了一台 ThinkPad X1 Carbon，这个机器质感还不错的，我把它当成真机环境，设置永不休眠，可以让我和我的Agent 24 小时去验证测试回归，包括获取各种真实系统环境的参数验证，400 多款 Windows 软件的卸载、残留清理、注册表、启动项测试，大部分在虚拟机里跑，x64 安装包、真实的高分屏、电池、SmartScreen 这些虚拟机看得不准确的，就直接放到这台机器上验，所以这台机器让我感觉也非常值。

然后为了不想在两台机器拷来拷去，最后还是用了 UU 远程，直接在 ThinkPad 那边开一个远程终端，我这边在 Mac 上直接操作，然后还把 ssh 连接当做备用，大部分软件的安装、卸载和调试，都是通过命令行脚本去完成的，剩下需要看界面的，直接通过远程桌面让 computer use 去操作，非常方便，最终相当于我还是在 Mac 上做的所有的事情。

差不多就是这些啦，这个过程下来，到最后成品让几个 Mole 天使用户去试用，大伙用着很爽，感觉这个过程的开发非常值，很有意思，而且可以帮助大家解决不少痛点，加上 Windows 上小白用户应该比 Mac 要多不少，让他们也享受到好软件的体验其实很值得开心。

差不多这两天这两篇文章算是把我这一个月的思考和想法聊完了，欢迎交流，有在做 Windows 开发的小伙伴也可以一起聊聊你们的最佳实践，假如还有空，下一篇我想着给大伙聊聊怎么在研发过程中借其他程序语言的生态来补桌面端的短板，这里也非常有意思。

one model for everything costs you.

a workflow that did the rounds last week routes every stage to a different model: a research assistant for planning, one model for day-to-day coding and debugging, a cheaper sibling for writing and running tests, the heavier one again for frontend and design. the same week, people running Gemini 4 Argon reported it ahead of both OpenAI and Claude models on document creation, data analysis and reasoning, while the coding crowd stayed elsewhere.

the pattern is the same in both: the best model for the job changes by the job.

the default that costs you: picking one flagship, pointing it at everything, and paying flagship prices for work a cheaper model does as well. tests, formatting, first drafts, summaries. those rarely need the top tier.

what I do: write the task list first, then assign a model to each line based on what it needs. reasoning-heavy and high-stakes gets the flagship. volume and latency-sensitive gets the cheap one. anything with a reference answer gets the cheap one plus a check.

the verification step: run the same task on both tiers once and diff the outputs. if you can't tell them apart, you were overpaying.

I built a prompt that does this mapping for your actual job. it asks what you do all week and returns a 30-day plan of which tasks go to which tool.

Gemini 4 Argon became available to Pro users in Antigravity this month.

the prompt that maps your real week to the right tools:

text:
今天安全领域的整个时间线上都是两件大事，对所有的互联网用户和产品应该都有影响。

第一个是有个印度证书颁发机构用了一个非常容易被猜到的数字当做私钥：

强度极弱，基本上任何人都能猜出来。

其中一个私钥就是个位数"4"，原本长达七十多位的密钥变成了单个数字 4；剩下的也是 56、66、115、155 这种数字。

这相当于给保险柜设了个密码"4"，试不到十下就能试出来。

更离谱的是，多次审计居然都没发现这几个私钥有问题。

目前 Chrome 和 Firefox 已经在几个小时内把这些私钥拉黑了，官方也把这 8 个私钥全部吊销。

真是很难想象这个机构草台班子到了什么程度。

现在浏览器端是安全的，但非浏览器端可能需要排查一下，尤其是你自己的项目如果涉及类似证书，建议让 AI 帮忙查一下。

第二个是严重 PHP 漏洞：

这个漏洞极其严重，官方说唯一真正安全的做法是立刻升级，但很多老旧网页已经多年没有升级过了。
更关键的是，有研究人员在 PHP 官方还没修复漏洞的情况下就直接公开了细节，导致所有人都能利用它发起攻击。

该漏洞是 OpenAI 资助的 Patch the Plane 项目用 GPT-5.6 Sol 发现的，无需登录即可远程拿下服务器。

漏洞覆盖面极大，比如大量依赖 PHP 的 WordPress 站点都会受到攻击。

目前荷兰议会、荷兰国家安全中心、芬兰中央政府网站，以及日本著名的 Pixiv 应用都因此关闭了一段时间。

感觉 AI 出来以后，攻防对抗变得异常剧烈，漏洞暴露和修复的频率都极快。

OpenAI 还表示，他们已经发现了更多具有这种规模效应的漏洞。
全世界 70% 的网站都是 PHP 的，所以这个漏洞的影响真的很大

AI agents can reason over enormous amounts of information, but much of the world's actual work is still trapped in PDFs, spreadsheets, scans, and other formats that models struggle to reliably understand.

Reducto co-founder and CEO Adit Abraham argues that solving this document layer is essential if agents are going to take on consequential work in healthcare, legal, finance, and insurance.

Adit joins a16z General Partner Jennifer Li to explain why traditional OCR breaks down on messy real-world documents, how Reducto combines vision-language models with specialized infrastructure to reach high accuracy without sacrificing cost or latency, and why frontier models can silently drop information on long extraction tasks.

Reducto now processes billions of pages each month, and crossed its 7 billionth page the morning of this recording.

We formally announced Mirendil less than 4 months ago. Today, I'm excited to share an important milestone for:

Pretraining at scale without a pretraining team.

Mirendil's mission is to solve Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) and use it to democratize frontier AI development, ultimately accelerating science and technology. At Mirendil, when we think about RSI, we think holistically about the company as an intelligent entity that self-improves toward its goal. From that perspective, the most powerful notion of acceleration is reducing the time and resources (number of human experts, compute, and other costs) needed to achieve ambitious goals.

Given that pretraining is perhaps the most important yet most challenging part of frontier AI development, we decided to run an ambitious controlled experiment: Starting fully from scratch, can we significantly reduce the time, number of human experts, and compute resources needed to go all the way to successfully pretraining a strong coding model at scale?

Mirendil-Base is the result of this experiment. Our first pretrained model was built by one researcher in 3.5 months, with less than $10M in compute. This includes all the research and small-scale experiments it took to get there, as well as the final training run.

The recipe holds up as the models get bigger. For reference, Mirendil-Base is in the 100B-500B parameter range, Mirendil-Base-Large in the 500B-2T range, and Mirendil-Base-XL in the 2T-10T range.

We're beginning to see a world where a single researcher, empowered by AI, can take on work that once required an entire research organization. As these systems improve, the bottleneck shifts from the size of a team to the ambition and judgment of the people directing them. This has profound implications for who gets to build AI and, ultimately, who gets to push the frontiers of science and technology forward.

We’ll share independent evaluations, post-training benchmarks and API-access sooner than you think so stay tuned!

text:
Adit Abraham of @reductoai on why everything in AI is "state-of-the-art all the time," and how to find what actually works for you:

"One of the unfortunate things about the AI industry... is benchmarks have become marketing over time."

"There's a public benchmark out there that we tested where if you take the same documents and you add a little bit of noise, like you tilt it one degree, you add a little Gaussian blur, the provider that published the benchmark gets way, way worse than everyone else, but everyone else is kind of consistent."

"Our recommendation is actually LLM as a judge is quite strong today if you're thoughtful about how you think about a rubric and how to approach it."

"We want to see the industry move closer to people testing on their own data, with tools maybe to make that evaluation easier."

"Instead of trusting a generic benchmark, you really should be at a point where you know what works best for you."

Today we’re releasing Underdog Bark 3.0, the #1 frontier speech model

It's a tiny 163 MB download as accurate as NVIDIA’s Parakeet (15x bigger). It beats OpenAI's Whisper large-v3 (57x bigger)

It's fast- transcribes 1 min of audio in <0.25s on a Macbook. On recorded meetings (AMI), Bark 3.0 gets 7.82% of words wrong. Parakeet gets 9.42%. OpenAI's Whisper large-v3 gets 13.63% error rate

Bark runs on both your Laptop & Phone. It’s free and open source under CC-BY 4.0

Try private on-device meeting notes & dictation, powered by Bark, in Underdog today: http://underdog.ai/bark

We formally announced Mirendil less than 4 months ago. Today, I'm excited to share an important milestone for:

Pretraining at scale without a pretraining team.

Mirendil's mission is to solve Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) and use it to democratize frontier AI development, ultimately accelerating science and technology. At Mirendil, when we think about RSI, we think holistically about the company as an intelligent entity that self-improves toward its goal. From that perspective, the most powerful notion of acceleration is reducing the time and resources (number of human experts, compute, and other costs) needed to achieve ambitious goals.

Given that pretraining is perhaps the most important yet most challenging part of frontier AI development, we decided to run an ambitious controlled experiment: Starting fully from scratch, can we significantly reduce the time, number of human experts, and compute resources needed to go all the way to successfully pretraining a strong coding model at scale?

Mirendil-Base is the result of this experiment. Our first pretrained model was built by one researcher in 3.5 months, with less than $10M in compute. This includes all the research and small-scale experiments it took to get there, as well as the final training run.

The recipe holds up as the models get bigger. For reference, Mirendil-Base is in the 100B-500B parameter range, Mirendil-Base-Large in the 500B-2T range, and Mirendil-Base-XL in the 2T-10T range.

We're beginning to see a world where a single researcher, empowered by AI, can take on work that once required an entire research organization. As these systems improve, the bottleneck shifts from the size of a team to the ambition and judgment of the people directing them. This has profound implications for who gets to build AI and, ultimately, who gets to push the frontiers of science and technology forward.

We’ll share independent evaluations, post-training benchmarks and API-access sooner than you think so stay tuned!
Read more about this milestone here: https://mirendil.com/news/pretraining-at-scale-without-a-pretraining-team/
